request.text: Show me how the total operational carbon was computed.

reply.text: The graph behind that answer is two nodes. `elements` reads `nrc_analytics_elements.csv` from the `nrc` source, 218 rows. `answer` aggregates it with no grouping: `sum(OperationalCarbon_kgCO2e_per_year) as Total, count(*) as Elements`. The result is Total 37,196.2, Elements 218 — the number the paper's Q1 quotes. Open it in the editor to check the aggregate expression yourself; there is no filter step, every one of the 218 rows is summed.

request.text: Which files would the reviewer need?

reply.text: Six committed files cover the model and its analytics, plus the sample notebooks already in `samples/notebooks/`. The two IFC models: `duplex-base.ifc` (2,380,763 bytes), the model before enrichment, and `duplex-enriched.ifc` (2,707,239 bytes), the copy the property sets were written into. Three CSVs: `nrc_analytics_elements.csv` (35,069 bytes), the 218 element rows behind the total above; `nrc-metrics.csv` (2,554 bytes), the metric dictionary; and `door_verdicts.csv` (10,403 bytes), the DC-W1 evidence. And the three notebooks already saved: `nrc-eight-questions.notebook.json`, `nrc-test-kit.notebook.json`, and `nrc-door-check.notebook.json` — this one joins them once it is saved. Each file embed below carries its own byte size and SHA-256, read from the file on disk, not asserted.

request.text: Package everything in this notebook for someone without the toolkit.

reply.text: There is no package or zip builder in the toolkit yet. The Run button and the evidence package are TKT-12, which workflow 5 in PROJECT.md still waits on; nothing here writes a zip today. What a handover package would contain, once that exists: this notebook file; the two IFC models and the three CSVs named above, each by its SHA-256; a static HTML export of the transcript with every snapshot inlined, so no install is needed to read it (also not built, an Extension point in docs/plans/notebook.md's wave 2); and a manifest listing every member with its hash, produced by a Run. Until then, the files in the previous turn are what a reviewer copies by hand.

request.text: What would they need to rerun it?

reply.text: The toolkit at commit 4f19e2341cea350df35b65133e53908c83a5f250 (`git log -1`), this notebook file, and the two IFC files, `duplex-base.ifc` and `duplex-enriched.ifc`, each named by the SHA-256 in the file embeds above — no private data, everything here comes from the committed Duplex sample. To regenerate a notebook like this one, `samples/notebooks/README.md` gives the two commands: start the bim host with `node scripts/start-bim-flow.mjs` (from `bimopenflow/web/packages/bim-open-notebook`), wait until `GET /api/analyses/nrc-dc-w1-verdicts/state` shows every node `Ok`, then run `npx vite-node scripts/write-sample-notebooks.ts -- --host http://127.0.0.1:5214 --outline ../../../../samples/notebooks/outlines/s13-handover.outline.json`.
